findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: email_check, fetch, search · Private data: company, defi_yields, domain, ens, evm_address, evm_balance, evm_token_balance, evm_token_risk, evm_tx, news_search, token_price, token_report, token_risk, tokens_trending, wallet · Public sink: company, email_check, ens, news_search, rss, token_risk.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: email_check, fetch, search · Private data: company, defi_yields, domain, ens, evm_address, evm_balance, evm_token_balance, evm_token_risk, evm_tx, news_search, token_price, token_report, token_risk, tokens_trending, wallet · Public sink: company, email_check, ens, news_search, rss, token_risk

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
